summary: Halyard mutual NDA with Veridian Cloud, Inc. whose edits are mostly US spelling and entity details, but the counterparty asks for a shorter survival period and a change of governing law, and adds independent contractors as Representatives.

findings.quote: VERIDIAN CLOUD, INC.]], a company incorporated and registered in [[INS: the State of Delaware, United States of America]]
findings.why: The counterparty has completed its entity name, Delaware incorporation and principal office; this is an entity-detail correction for the lawyer to check against the company register.

findings.quote: each Party may disclose certain Confidential Information to the other Party
findings.why: The agreement is genuinely mutual: Disclosing Party and Receiving Party are defined by role so either party can be either, and obligations run to both.

findings.quote: which is either marked or identified as confidential at the time of disclosure or would reasonably be considered confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of its disclosure
findings.why: Definition is limited to information disclosed in connection with the Purpose, covers marked or reasonably confidential information, and includes derived notes and analyses.

findings.quote: not use or exploit the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in any way except solely for the Purpose
findings.why: Use is limited solely to the Purpose, defined in Recital (A) as discussions regarding a potential commercial relationship.

findings.quote: can demonstrate by written records or other reasonable evidence
findings.why: All four carve-outs (public domain not via breach, already held, third-party receipt, independent development) are present and unnarrowed, with a written records or reasonable evidence standard.

findings.quote: [[INS: independent contractors,]]
findings.why: The counterparty adds independent contractors to Representatives, which the PB05 preferred list (employees, officers, directors, advisers, auditors, insurers, Group) does not include and no ACCEPTABLE line covers, although clause 4.1 keeps need-to-know, written obligations and full liability.
findings.draft_redline: Representatives means, in relation to a Party, the employees, officers, directors, professional advisers, auditors and insurers of that Party and of any member of its Group.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would prefer to keep the Representatives definition to employees, officers, directors, advisers, auditors and insurers. If you need to share information with a particular contractor, please let us know and we can consider it case by case.

findings.quote: those of its Representatives and members of its Group who strictly need to know such Confidential Information
findings.why: Disclosure to Representatives and Group members is permitted on a need-to-know basis and the Receiving Party remains fully liable for them under 4.1.3.

findings.quote: Before making any disclosure pursuant to Clause 5.1, the Receiving Party shall, to the extent that it is legally permitted to do so:
findings.why: Compelled disclosure is permitted, notice and cooperation apply only where legally permitted, and resisting disclosure is at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: within ten Business Days of receipt of such request
findings.why: Ten Business Days, officer-signed confirmation, and a backup and legally-required copies exception with retained copies staying confidential.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information, and all intellectual property rights in or relating to it, shall remain the exclusive property of the Disclosing Party
findings.why: Ownership stays with the Disclosing Party and no licence is granted beyond use for the Purpose.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information is provided by the Disclosing Party on an "as is" basis.
findings.why: Information is provided as is with no warranty, no reliance liability except fraud, and no obligation to proceed.

findings.quote: Neither Party shall make, or permit any person to make, any public announcement, press release or other public disclosure
findings.why: Mutual restriction on announcements without prior written consent, except as required by law.

findings.quote: that Party shall not disclose such personal data unless and until the Parties have agreed and entered into a separate written data processing agreement or data sharing agreement
findings.why: Only business contact details are anticipated and any other personal data requires a separate DPA or data sharing agreement first.

findings.quote: for a period of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party giving not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice
findings.why: Agreement term of 2 years with 30 days' notice to terminate early, as preferred.

findings.quote: survive the expiry or termination of this Agreement for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of expiry or termination, save that in respect of any Confidential Information that constitutes a Trade Secret
findings.why: Survival of 3 years with Trade Secrets protected while they remain Trade Secrets is the preferred position; the counterparty comment asks to reduce this to 2 years, which RQ01 allows while keeping Trade Secret protection.

findings.quote: a Party shall be entitled to seek the remedies of injunction, specific performance and other equitable relief
findings.why: Mutual right to seek equitable relief, with cumulative remedies in 11.2.

findings.quote: Neither Party may assign, novate, transfer, mortgage, charge, subcontract, declare a trust over or deal in any other manner with any or all of its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other Party.
findings.why: Mutual prohibition on assignment without prior written consent.

findings.quote: not reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble or otherwise attempt to derive the composition, source code or underlying structure of any software, prototypes or other tangible objects
findings.why: Reverse engineering of software and prototypes is prohibited.

findings.quote: A person who is not a party to this Agreement shall not have any rights under the Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999
findings.why: Boilerplate is customary: third-party rights excluded, entire-agreement clause does not exclude fraud liability, and the DocuSign/Adobe Sign and courier edits are routine (RQ06 e-signature already permitted).

findings.quote: shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the law of England and Wales.
findings.why: The clause itself keeps English law, but the counterparty comment asks for Delaware or New York law or silence on governing law and venue, which is a request to change governing law that the playbook says to decline.
findings.draft_redline: This Agreement and any dispute or claim (including non-contractual disputes or claims) arising out of or in connection with it or its subject matter or formation shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the law of England and Wales, and the courts of England and Wales shall have non-exclusive jurisdiction.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We are not able to move away from English law for this NDA. As a compromise we can offer English law with non-exclusive jurisdiction, so that either party may bring proceedings elsewhere where needed to enforce its rights.
